characters.name: The Park Crew in General
characters.description: Aerith and Bob: They are evenly balanced with uncommon names (Pops, Skips, and Hi-Five Ghost) and more common names (Mordecai, Benson, and Rigby, which were relatively common particularly in the early 20th century). There is alsoThomas(another common name)whose real name is Nikolai (a common Slavic name), and Muscle Man is somewhere in the middle ashe is mostly referred to by his nickname, but his real name is Mitch. Arc Hero: Starting in season 3, every member of the Park Crew except High Five Ghost began to have important story arcs, and one would become important in a season or two.Mordecai: In seasons 3 and 4, Mordecai gradually develops his relationship with Margaret, and at the end of season 4, he was ready to ask her to be his girlfriend, but unfortunately, Margaret was accepted into college and they broke up, then, halfway through season 5, after reuniting with CJ, he slowly begins to fall in love with her and starts to forget about Margaret. Unfortunately, after Margaret's return in season 6, it becomes a love triangle for Mordecai until his breakup with CJ at Muscle Man's wedding in the season 6 finale..Pops: In seasons 7 and 8, the true origins of Pops and his legacy begin to be revealed, culminating in his training for the battle that will decide the fate of the universe. Mordecai: In seasons 3 and 4, Mordecai gradually develops his relationship with Margaret, and at the end of season 4, he was ready to ask her to be his girlfriend, but unfortunately, Margaret was accepted into college and they broke up, then, halfway through season 5, after reuniting with CJ, he slowly begins to fall in love with her and starts to forget about Margaret. Unfortunately, after Margaret's return in season 6, it becomes a love triangle for Mordecai until his breakup with CJ at Muscle Man's wedding in the season 6 finale.. Pops: In seasons 7 and 8, the true origins of Pops and his legacy begin to be revealed, culminating in his training for the battle that will decide the fat

characters.name: Mordecai
characters.description: A tall, art school drop-out blue jay who works with his friend Rigby at the park. Between the two, Mordecai is the more mature, although he will sometimes play along with the more enthusiastic Rigby's hijinks. Accidental Murder: In "It's Time". After getting rattled up all day by Rigby about him getting a date with Margaret and Mordecai not because of his shyness as well as his unwillingness to admit being jealous, Mordecai ends up pushing him out ofthe tunnel they're going through, killing him. He's remorseful afterwards. Aesop Amnesia: Despite having aJerkass Realizationregarding Rigby in "Death Punchies", he still mistreats him from time to time in subsequent episodes. Affectionate Nickname: His friends occasionally call him "Mordo", and there's also "Mordy" by his mother and Uncle Steve. Always Someone Better:Played With. Mordecai is better than Rigby in most aspects: way more friendly with people, more of a case of wasted talent than a deadbeat like Rigby, and considered more responsible than him. However, this only ends up making Rigby feel resentful and insecure. Ironically, Season 7 has Rigby himself becoming more successful than him, whether in romance or personal goals.

characters.name: Rigby
characters.description: A short raccoon, Mordecai's best friend since childhood, and his closest co-worker as a result. Being energetic and immature, he's usually the one who instigates any sort of trouble that Mordecai or the other characters get into. He is a high school drop-out who never received his diploma.Has avery tall younger brothernamed Don, an accountant who is favored by everyone. Adults Dressed as Children: Type A in "Fuzzy Dice". When the park workers need a kid to get inside aSuck E. Cheese'scenter, they have Rigby wear a hoodie, a fanny pack, and a backward cap due to his size. Alliterative Name: Rigby the Raccoon. All Men Are Perverts: Zig-zagged. The only reason he didn't want to see "Pajama Sisters 2" is because "They're just gonna talk about their feelings —fully clothed", yet in "The Unicorns Have Got to Go," he didn't see the appeal of having sexy women tearing a man's clothes off as seen in the Dude Time cologne commercial. He's also notably a better friend to Margaret than Mordecai, simply because he's able to treat her like a normal person. Aloof Big Brother: One to his brother Don. Namely because Don wastaller, stronger, and smarter than Rigby. He briefly crossed over intoBig Brother Bullyas well bytelling Don he wished he was never born. They patched things up, though.

characters.name: Benson
characters.description: An anthropomorphic gumball machine who is Mordecai and Rigby's boss. Although he generally seems mildly annoyed, at the worst he can get really pissed if Mordecai and/or Rigby have messed something up. All Drummers Are Animals: Subverted in "150-Piece Kit" when the audience finds out that the man behind Hair to the Throne's famous drum solo wasBenson. Animate Inanimate Object: He's a talking gumball machine. Anti-Villain:Sometimes, but when he is, he's a type IV (Villain In Name Only). Benson treats Mordecai and Rigby like crap most of the time, but he's just doing his job as their manager, although he's quite unreasonable. Though the duo tend to slack off a lot, they do nothing out of malicious intent. In truth, though, he can beNot So Above It Allat times and he's partially this way because his boss Pops Maellard is aScatterbrained Seniorwho isThe Alleged Boss, but delegates work to Benson, and aClueless Bosswho hasNo Social Skillsand isInnocently Insensitive, which causes him no end of stress in addition to hisFreudian Excusefor having aHair-Trigger Temper. Ax-Crazy: When hisHair-Trigger Temperreaches its limits, he can get quite violent.

characters.name: Pops
characters.description: The son of the park's wealthy owner who's been sheltered all his life. He's the group'sPlucky Comic Relief. Achievements in Ignorance: When Pops tries to get on his favorite game show, "Win That Prize", he instead ends up becoming the man that brings a television company back on top even getting promoted up to Senior Senior Vice President. The Alleged Boss: He's technically the boss of the park but rarely asserts his position and acts more like a co-worker. In a flashback, it's revealed that Mr. Maellard put Benson in chargespecificallybecause he knows perfectly well that his son is way too scatter-brained to handle the responsibility of maintaining the park. All-Loving Hero: Pops is a friendly and sweet person who never wants to harm anyone if he doesn't have to. Animal Motifs: Butterflies. He likes chasing them and they become more prevalent to him in season 8.

characters.name: Skips
characters.description: A yeti who also works at the park. He seems the most tolerant of the crazies he works with, and is often quick to find a solution to any problem. Absurd Phobia: His Halloween tale in "Terror Tales of the Park VI" reveals he has an unnatural fear… of flying disc freestylers.Skips:They're wobbly and unpredictable. Who knows where that disc will end up? The Ace: Most of the time. He's been adventuring and fighting evil for over 100 years. He even won an arm wrestling battle againstThe Grim Reaper. Achilles' Heel: Unmanaged stress. This is the one singular thing that is shown to be lethal to Skips in spite of his immortality, with him needing the help of all his friends to be able to defeat it. Beast and Beauty: Seen with hisinterspecies romancewith Mona.

characters.name: Muscle Man
characters.description: An ironically-named, short, out-of-shape guy, who has a hicklike lifestyle and constantly makes "My mom" jokes. The Ace: He's presented this way in "My Mom". He has a bunch of friends, Benson respects him, and he's an all-around cool guy to hang out with. Achilles in His Tent: In "Prankless", after one of his pranks nearly kills Pops. However, he brings himself out of the tent just in time to save the park. Acrofatic: There are times, especially during an episode's climax, where Muscle Man shows this. Despite his short and fat build, he isvery strong. And as shown in "Slam Dunk" he's actually a good athlete, when he smokes Mordecai and Rigby at basketball. Several times. Alliterative Name:MuscleMan.

characters.name: Hi-Five Ghost
characters.description: Muscle Man's ghost-looking best friend who hi-fives him a lot. Affectionate Nickname: His friends often refer to him as Fives. Ascended Extra: Since season 2, he has had more regular appearances. Babies Ever After:He and Celia have a son together by the series finale. Big Man on Campus: "New Bro on Campus" shows that HFG became instantly popular at the high school he and Muscle Man attended. In fact, in one day, he became more popular than Muscle Man, who was this trope himself.

characters.name: Mr. Maellard
characters.description: The owner of the park and the father of Pops. Accidental Misnaming: He keeps getting Benson's name wrong by calling him Beancan, Bert, Beanbag, Ball Bucket, Beanton, Bean Teen, and Beanson. By the end of "Benson Be Gone", he finally gets Benson's name correct, which sticks for future appearances. Ambiguously Evil: He's shown developing very suspicious plans for the Park throughout the seventh season that ultimatelysends the whole thing into space. In theFinale Season,we discover he wasGood All Along: he was preparing them to save the universe from Anti-Pops. Conspicuous Consumption: When he makes a mess of his limousine's upholstery he just buys a whole new limousine rather than have it cleaned. Cool Car: He is driven around in a white limousine called "The White Stallion" that's equipped with machine guns, tire spikes, mini missiles, wheel spikes, grapple guns, lasers, and a massive missile.

characters.name: Margaret Smith
characters.description: A red-breasted robin who used to work at the Coffee Shop, then later leaves town for college and becomes a news reporter after returning. Mordecai has a huge crush on her, though can’t find the courage to properly ask her out. Affectionate Nickname: "Hug Bug" from her father. All Girls Want Bad Boys: The only time Margaret has shown to have an interest in Mordecai was when he "blew her off" (Mordecai at the time was suffering aHeroic BSoDfrom seeing Pops naked). Eventually inverted around Season 3. Amicable Exes:Zigzaggedwith Mordecai. After they broke up and she returns home to find out he’s now with CJ, it is awkward, as Mordecai has complicated feelings over seeing her again while being in an official relationship. Things gets even messier after they share a kiss. And while they have no ill will for one another, Mordecai's awkward nature initially causes some problems, but they manage to work it out, especially when they’re forced to confront their feelings and agree to just be friends. Unlike CJ, the writers confirmed she and Mordecai are still friends in the future. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: In most episodes, though in some she does wear shoes.

characters.name: Cloudy Jay "CJ"
characters.description: A cloud girl who Mordecai goes on a blind date with after thinking Margaret was engaged and befriends as a result. In Season 5 they wind up reuniting, becoming friends and then dating. Action Girl:In "Dodge This". Despite her team being rookies, they make it all the way to the finals of the dodgeball tournament andend up winning the whole thing. She even beats Mordecai, the park's best player, one on one after they work things out.She even saved him and Rigby, with Eileen's help, in "Portable Toilet". In "Dodge This". Despite her team being rookies, they make it all the way to the finals of the dodgeball tournament andend up winning the whole thing. She even beats Mordecai, the park's best player, one on one after they work things out. She even saved him and Rigby, with Eileen's help, in "Portable Toilet". Amicable Exes:Avertedwith Mordecai. While they ended their relationship on amicable terms, even hugging one another during their last conversation before she leaves, CJ is (understandably) a little frosty to Mordecai (apparently in the storyboards for "Rigby's Graduation Day Special" she was supposed to roll her eyes after seeing the Park Dome launch into space) and the creators confirmed they no longer speak with each other post-breakup or anytime in the future.

characters.name: Final Episode Character
characters.description: An artist and Mordecai's future wife. All There in the Manual: Her name was revealed from the creators on an AMA reddit page. Babies Ever After: Had two sons and one daughter with Mordecai. Boyish Short Hair: Sports this as an older woman during the 25 year park reunion. Clingy Jealous Girl: Slightly in the "25 Years Later" comic, but justified as Mordecai and she are married and seeing him aged down back to his 20s (Long story) and hanging with a likewise de-aged Margret didn't help matters. Mordecai assures her however any feelings for Margret are long by the wayside and he would never betray her.

characters.name: Eileen Roberts
characters.description: Anadorkablysweet mole girl who works at the coffee shop with Margaret. Has a crush on Rigby, which he initially is annoyed by, but gradually starts to warm up to her. Action Survivor: Proves herself to be one of these in "Camping Can Be Cool". Without her, Mordecai, Margaret and Rigby would probably not have made it out of those woods alive... Ascended Extra: Went from Margaret's best friend to one of Mordecai and Rigby's closest companions before officially joining the main cast in the eighth season. Author Avatar: Eileen is basically Minty Lewis in mole form. Her biggest roles are generally in episodes Minty Lewis (who's a writer on the show) co-wrote with Kat Morris. Babies Ever After:She and Rigby have two daughters in the series finale.

characters.name: Starla Gutsmandottir
characters.description: Muscle Man's on again-off again (currently on) girlfriend and later wife. Acrofatic: Much like her boyfriend/husband, she's surprisingly quick and agile despite being fat. Affectionate Nickname: "Babe" from Muscle Man. Alliterative Name: Post-marriage with Mitch:StarlaSorenstein. Amazing Technicolor Population: Green skin like Muscle Man.

characters.name: Celia
characters.description: A human girl Hi-Five Ghost met four years ago before she went off to study in Prague, Czech Republic. Ascended Extra: Appears in five episodes in the show (Her introduction, a Christmas episode, Muscle Man and Starla's wedding, a Halloween story and the finale). She plays a major role in theAdventure Time x Regular Showcomic crossover. Babies Ever After:She and Hi-Five Ghost have a son together by the series finale. Birds of a Feather: With Hi-Five Ghost. They love the same coffee shop, down-tempo electronica, the same music album, watching animals in the aquarium, and they don't like the food in Wing Kingdom. But unfortunately, none of them had cellphones back then. Boyish Short Hair: Has naturally brown hair in an undercut with a longer fringe on top dyed teal.

characters.name: Audrey
characters.description: Benson's next-door neighbor and girlfriend. 555: Her phone number starts with the titular numbers. Amicable Exes: Kinda. While she did invite her ex-boyfriend to her party, her ex tries to prevent anyone from dating her. Flat Character: She doesn't get many changes to her personality as the show progresses. Girl Next Door: She's Benson's next-door neighbor and aSatellite Love Interestfor him.

characters.name: Pam
characters.description: One of the dome scientists, who Benson develops a crush on and later a relationship with. Back for the Finale:She came back and worked with Benson after Mordecai and Rigby left. Birds of a Feather: With Benson, as both of them are workaholics and love chicken wings. Brainy Brunette: Pam has brown hair and is one of the dome scientists. Crash-Into Hello: With Benson at the start of "Pam I Am".

characters.name: Desdemona "Mona"
characters.description: Skip's deceased love and girlfriend. Beast and Beauty: Was a beautiful woman who falled in love with Skips who is a yeti. Conspicuous Gloves: She wore black fingerless lace gloves as a fashion choice. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her debut episode, "Diary,thisis what she looked like. Flowers of Femininity: She wore a hat filled with flowers.

characters.name: Hilary and William
characters.description: Mordecai's parents. They both love their son, even if Mordecai is usually embarrassed by his mother. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Ever since he was a teenager, Hilary has always unintentionally embarrassed Mordecai whenever he brings a girl home, which ends with them leaving. She even put together a whole home movie of Mordecai's most embarrassing moments titled "Mordy Moments". CJ however wasn’t put off by any of it, thinking she’s sweet, and Mordecai learns to appreciate her as she’s genuinely been a good parent to him. Cannot Tell a Lie: They both attribute this as to why their marriage has been going strong for twenty five years - unless Hilary asks if she can still pass as a college student. It’s also the advice Hilary gives Mordecai over how to solve his issues with CJ in "Sad Sax". Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Hilaryhad blue feathers on her forehead and a different hairstylein her debut appearance in The Thanksgiving Episode, and she wore a salmon dress (the latter was likely because it was a special occasion). Eye Glasses: William has these.

characters.name: Don
characters.description: Rigby's younger brother who's also an accountant. The Ace: Tall, uber nice, drives a wicked car, and loved by all. Always Someone Better: To Rigby, which is the reason why Rigby resents him. Animals Not to Scale: He'shuge. Annoying Younger Sibling:While he isn't doing it on purpose to Rigby, Rigby resents his brother because everyone likes him more and he's more successful.

characters.name: Sherm and Barbera
characters.description: Abusive Dad: Sherm is of the emotionally abusive variety regarding Rigby. He usually lets his short temper out on him and makes it verbally clear that he sees him as a screw up. Even when Rigby was little he was shown telling him his ideas for playing together were terrible and to not interrupt his tv time. Brutal Honesty: Sherm does not sugarcoat how much he thinks abysmally of Rigby in almost every appearance he makes. Calling the Old Man Out: Sherm is on the receiving end of this from Rigby in the episode "Rigby Goes to the Prom".Rigby:(in the front passenger seat of his father's car with Eileen and Sherm about to fall off a cliff, as Sherm continues to blame him)Gah, Dad, STOP! It doesn't matter if I ever get a big job or my G.E.D., you'restillnever gonna trust me, and that's on YOU! You're so focused on your car, you never noticed me growing up! Also, it's totallyyourfault 'cause you were the one driving and you weren't watching the road! NOW GIMME THE WHEEL! Character Development: Sherm slowly comes around and starts to show more respect to Rigby when the latter goes through his ownCharacter Developmentof becoming more responsible and finishing high school. Disappointed in You: His main attitude to Rigby, though not without reason.

characters.name: "Muscle Dad" Sorenstein
characters.description: Muscle Man's late father. All of the Other Reindeer: He was a forklift operator who longed to be a trucker, with the truckers looking down on him and picking on him. Always Someone Better: His children manage to pursue and succeed at his interests more than he ever could. Amazing Technicolor Population: He has green skin just like his wife and son. Big Damn Heroes: Saves his son, Mordecai and Rigby from an army ofJerkasstruckers from beyond the grave.

characters.name: Monique "Muscle Mom" Sorenstein
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: She has green skin. Big Beautiful Woman: She has a heavyset build with noticeable curves, and she has a gentle face to go with it. Killed Offscreen:Regular Show: 25 Years Laterimplies that she has passed away by the time of theDistant Finale. Minor Major Character: Muscle Man talks about her a lot, yet she's only appeared twice in the show. The Prankster: She scares her sons with a scary costume every Halloween.

characters.name: John "Muscle Bro" Sorenstein
characters.description: A truck driver, and Muscle Man's older brother. Characterization Marches On: Starts off very antagonistic to anyone that wasn't his brother, before becoming friendlier in later appearances. Escaped from Hell: How he's introduced in "My Mom" — by driving his truck straight out of the underworld. Foil: To his brother, Muscle Man. Both of them have similar builds and are pranksters, but Muscle Bro lacks his brother's other personality traits that make him more tolerable, thought that may be due to his lack of screentime. Muscle Man also shares their father's hobbies the most, while Muscle Bro mainly manages to become a trucker like his father always wanted to be. Horrifying the Horror: He may be tough and sadistic in his pranks, but he's always been scared of the prank Muscle Mom pulls every Halloween.

characters.name: Low-Five Ghost
characters.description: The older brother of Hi-Five Ghost who gives low-fives and he's also a police officer. Cool Big Bro: He's always willing to lend HFG a helping hand when asked. Cool Shades: He wears two types of sunglasses. He wears black Aviator sunglasses when he's cop and turquoise wayfarers sunglasses when he's off-duty. Dirty Cop: A benevolent example, he's not afraid to bend the rules to help out his brother and his friends. Heel–Face Turn:Zig-Zagged. He was in jail in his first appearance, but later became a cop after being bailed out. But, even after becoming a cop, he bends the rules to help his brother and his friends.

characters.name: Quintin "Quips" Quippenger
characters.description: A yeti who is Skips' cousin who constantly tells terrible jokes and gets on the nerves of everybody. Alliterative Name:QuintinQuippenger. Also applies with his nickname. Ambitious, but Lazy:Deconstructed. At least on the sympathy side. He really wants to become a comedian but never stops to think of how people would react to his (unintentionally) insulting jokes. Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and Yeti: Like his cousin, Quips is a yeti. Brilliant, but Lazy: He has good vocabulary skills for his jokes but doesn't think of how to use them in a way that doesn't insult others.

characters.name: Frank Smith
characters.description: The Channel Six traffic reporter, and Margaret's human father. Boyfriend-Blocking Dad: Frank acts cold and dismissive towards Mordecai for most of "Family BBQ", along with any other boyfriend Margaret has brought home, because he's afraid that he will lose his "Hug Bug". Character Development: Initially a hostileJerkassto Mordecai for dating Margaret, but comes to genuinely like him near the end of "Family BBQ". And Frank's subsequent appearances, which wereafterMordecai and Margaret broke up, Frank is more friendly to the former, even saying how Mordecai is a like a son to him. Interspecies Romance: His wife is a robin and he's a human. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Despite his initial hostility to Mordecai, he soon warms up to him.

characters.name: Commander Rawls
characters.description: The Commander of Space Tree Station, where the Park Crew ends up after being blasted into space. Ambiguously Evil: Keeps the true purpose of the SPARK initiative from the crew and dodges Benson's questions when confronted.Subverted as of "Space Escape": He only doesn't explain why Pops is important because there isn't time, and does everything in his power to protect the Park Crew. It's also made clear whatever the Park's mysterious mission is, it's a good one. Big Good: Of In Space.For the first third anyway. Drill Sergeant Nasty: A mild example, as he only puts on the persona to try and get Benson not to quit, and the worst he does most of the time is tell his crew to drop and give him 20. A Father to His Men: Willing to lay down his life for his men in a heartbeat. Also seeReasonable Authority FigureBellow.

characters.name: Chance Sureshot
characters.description: A bumbling Space Tree Ranger. Back from the Dead: Revived afterAnti-Pops' death. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl:Gender InvertedChance is the goofy, perky, fun, Gentle Guy to Sally's Brooding Babe. Butt-Monkey: His friends don't like him for being a tool and "Missing Wallet" ends with him still trapped after it's revealed his wallet had no money in it. Clone Army: It's later revealed thathe has an army of clones.

characters.name: Toothpick Sally
characters.description: Another Space Tree Ranger who constantly has a toothpick in her mouth. Action Girl: By far the strongest of the Space Ranger trio. Back from the Dead: Revived afterAnti-Pops' death. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl:Gender InvertedSally is the serious, stoic, cold, Brooding Babe to Chance's Gentle Guy. The Comically Serious: She keeps a stoic demeanor while accompanying the more bumbling Chance and the cast's misadventures.

characters.name: Recap Robot
characters.description: The final member of the Space Tree Ranger trio. A robot who provides helpful information. Back from the Dead:Revived after Anti-Pops' death. Beware the Nice Ones: Kind, helpful... and just as badass as his friends. Cute Machines: Anencouragingmachine with a screen to smile with. Mr. Exposition: For the Space Tree and for any planets the crew visits.

characters.name: Sensai
characters.description: The Death Kwon Do Instructor, Sensai, is an overweight martial arts instructor who teaches the fighting style of Death Kwon Do and is now a deli owner. Acrofatic: Despite his pudgier build, he's capable of performing devastating techniques from Death Kwon Do. Big "NO!": He lets it outthree timesin "Death Punchies", when Mordecai and Rigby steal from his Death Kwon Do book andwhen someone Death Kwon Clogged the toilet. Blatant Lies: Claims that his Sandwich of Health is a healthier option on his menu in "Death Kwon Do-Livery." After having eaten it daily, his stomach explodes the second he takes another bite. Body Horror: His Sandwich of Health causes his stomach to explode.

characters.name: The Guardians of Eternal Youth
characters.description: Supernatural beings resembling giant, floating babies. Responsible for granting Skips his immortality. They also enjoy cake. Absurdly Powerful Student Council: They were this in high school. And they were also the glee club. Babies Make Everything Better: Unless you anger one of them. Bargain with Heaven: Skips did one with them. It has harsh consequences if Skips fails to do a ritual every year on his birthday. Big Damn Heroes: They arrived to help the park workers in "Exit 9B".

characters.name: Gareth "Gary"
characters.description: The mysterious chauffeur for the Guardians of Youth. Absurdly Powerful Student Council: He was a member of the student counsel with the Guardians of Eternal Youth during high school. Big Damn Heroes: He arrived to help the park workers in his car in "Exit 9B". Cool Car: His flying El Camino. A Day in the Limelight: In the episode "Gary's Synthesizer"

characters.name: Baby Ducks
characters.description: A bunch of baby ducks that Mordecai and Rigby found in the park fountain. They imprinted on Rigby and started following him around and copied his actions. They are able to fuse together and transform into a giant human with a duck's head. All Your Powers Combined: When they transform into a giant. Armored Villains, Unarmored Heroes: In the first part of the fight, but it's subverted when they gain aPowered Armor. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: When they fuse together. Badass Adorable: Adorable duckies who can turn into a building-sized kicker of ass.

characters.name: God of Basketball
characters.description: The god of basketball who can also coach people on how to play basketball. Badass Cape: He always wears a golden cape. Berserk Button: Don't you dare bad-mouth basketball. Big Damn Heroes: He arrived to help the park workers in "Exit 9B". He comes back again in "Bank Shot" to tell Rigby that his "double or nothing" shot from early in the episode was still in play. Cool Car: He drives a custom designed white flying Cadillac Escalade.

characters.name: Techmo
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: He looks humanoid but he has green skin and pointy ears. Artificial Limbs: During the American Revolution, he lost his arm and Skips replaces it with a wooden arms. Centuries later, he upgrades his arm to a robotic version. Big Damn Heroes: He arrived to help the park workers in "Exit 9B". Call-Back: His robo-arm is made by Yoshimoto Cybernetics, the same company that makes thePlayco Arm Boy. Cool Car: He drives aDeLoreanDMC-12 and has a car specifically for storm chasing.

characters.name: Eggscellent Knight
characters.description: 24-Hour Armor: He is never seen in any other attire. Cool Old Guy: He's been active for over a thousand years, guarding treasures and artifacts that Mordecai and Rigby seek out. He's even willing to help them out as much as he can. Inexplicably Awesome: He mainly appears to guard and explain mythical artifacts and has none of his history ever explained. New Job as the Plot Demands: In "Eggscellent", he worked as somebody waiting for a winner of the Eggscellent Challenge, but because that only happens every 1,000 years, he spent the rest of his time in an old game store. By "Gamers Never Say Die", the game store had flown away, along with his job, so in "Garage Door," he now works in the House Warehouse. His final appearance is in "Ice Tape," where he is the guardian of the fire VCR, the ice VCR, and the seemingly normal VCR.

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: Badass Santa: Oh yes. Stops his head elf from creating a dangerous item from dark magic and when he goes behind his back to get it, Santa chases him down before crashing into the park and entrusting the gift for Mordecai and Rigby to dispose of. Big Fun: Somewhat averted. While a big guy, Santa is not fat at all and he is pretty grumpy throughout the episode.Justified, given the fact his head inventor made a supremely dangerous item and had to stop him.He loosens up a bit considerably when the job is done. Bulletproof Vest: How he survived getting shot by Quillgin. It also makes him look a bit rounder than he actually is, (especially with the sweater on.) Expecting Someone Taller: When Mordecai and Rigby first encounters him, they don't believe he's Santa due to his appearance not matching what everyone imagines. Santa says that TV producers made up his appearances. Hell-Bent for Leather: Wears a sweet leather longcoat over his holiday sweater.

characters.name: RGB2
characters.description: A talking robotic TV set and the star of the popular 80s sitcom,That's My Television. He actually wants to break free of stardom and seeks Mordecai and Rigby's help. And I Must Scream:He's been trapped in a mobile TV box for years and can only survive with a steady supply of air from the 80s. Judging by the timespan, he's been in that box since he wasa teenager. Catchphrase: Two cheesy sitcom ones: "I hope you saved room for dessert!" and "Hey, It's my turn to drive!" Celebrity is Overrated: Oh lord, like you'd never believe.RGB2's career was a miserable life of virtual slavery, confined to a small prison and forced to keep the act going to appease greedy TV executives and obsessive fans. Cool Old Guy: Well, he's been around since the 80sand he's a very old, decrepit man inside that TV. Nonetheless, he's a cheerful and friendly fellow.

characters.name: Roxy
characters.description: A floating rock who runs "Roxy's Famous Fries", a fry food truck that visits the Space Tree. Animate Inanimate Object: She's a living rock. The Cameo: Is mentioned briefly in "SpaceyMcSpaceTree" and Rigby being banned from her truck is the catalyst for him trying to find a way around his punishment.Rigby:Her butt salt is delicious! Human Resources: Uses salt from her own butt in the fries. Surprisingly, it's quite delicious. A Lizard Named "Liz": She's a sentient floating rock namedRoxy.

characters.name: Earl
characters.description: An old teacher the crew meet in spacesent to train Pops for his confrontation with Anti-Pops. Big Good: Earl takes up the role in the second half of season 8until his death at Anti-Pops' hands. He has trained all previous incarnations of Pops, and has tattoos all over his body for every time Pops and Anti-Pops fight. Likewise, for several episodes, Earl trains Pops and helps him get through the fact he has to fight his brother, explaining that he must defeat Anti-Pops or the universe will reset itself once again. Fan Disservice: To prove that he's not bluffing aboutthe universe being reset with every stalemate, he takes his robe off to show his many,manytattoos, which get applied every time it happens. Fourth-Wall Observer: In terms ofTraining Montages, where he's fully aware of what they're capable of while everyone at The Park remains confused by their effects. Fundoshi: Shown wearing one when he presents his tattoos.

characters.name: Party Pete (Peter Hermanverfal)
characters.description: A party entertainer that Mordecai and Rigby hired to help liven up their party. Back from the Dead:His clone is among the many villains to be brought back to life by Garrett Bobby Ferguson Jr. in "Exit 9B". Balloon Belly: After drinking several Radicolas which gave him strange powers. After finding out Benson was going to return to the park to see what all the commotion was about, the gang had to keep giving Party Pete Radicolas so he'll burn out in order to get rid of him before Benson showed up, thus ending Mordecai and Rigby's party with abang. Big Eater: Big Drinker, rather. He consumes several cans ofRadiColato the point where he expands and explodes. Cerebus Retcon: He originally started off as a one-off character in an early episode. By "Party Re-Pete," we find out thathe's really been held captive and cloned for his party-enhancing abilities.

characters.name: Death
characters.description: An undead soul collector and Skips' arch nemesis. Affably Evil: He genuinely cares about his family, always follows his word, and you kinda get the idea he's enjoying himself while playing these various games against Skips. Anti-Hero: He helped the gang defeat Garrett Bobby Ferguson, Jr. and his henchmen in "Exit 9B". Badass Biker: Death rides a supernatural motorcycle, and is definitely a badass. Big Damn Heroes: He arrived to help the park workers in "Exit 9B".

characters.name: Chad and Jeremy
characters.description: A possum and ostrich that Benson offers positions to when he plans to replace Mordecai and Rigby. Butt-Monkey: They both get antagonized by Mordecai and Rigby when they try and clean the boats. Extreme Doormat: Subverted. They're polite and may look likeGeeks, but they'renotpeople to be pushed around or is willing to submissive as Mordecai and Rigby find out the hard way after one of their failed sabotages gets exposed. Foil: To Mordecai and Rigby. While Mordecai and Rigby are a pair of two that work at the park, the two are slackers who go commando,frequently fight, have basic education at best, and usually only fight if the situation comes to it. Chad and Jeremy are fully clothed, take their work seriously, received degrees from The Institute of Technical Technology, appear to always agree with each other, and are likely to start a fight if pushed. Genius Bruiser: They graduated with degrees from The Institute of Technical Technology and are capable fighters who can match Mordecai and Rigby in aMirror Match.

characters.name: Gene
characters.description: A snack vending machine who's the park manager of East Pines park. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: In theBad Futuretimeline shown inthe Movie, Geneis revealed to be theleading the Galactic Park Rangersand turns up in the climax rallying the final assault on the Timenado.This is in contrast to Gene in the showwho appears to have never joined the Galactic Park Rangers or even gone into space at all following Season 7. Always Someone Better:He's a better park manager than Benson, able to win Park Manager of the Year several times in his career.He loves taking prank wars farther and farther, but he can never contend with Muscle Man. He's a better park manager than Benson, able to win Park Manager of the Year several times in his career. He loves taking prank wars farther and farther, but he can never contend with Muscle Man.

characters.name: Guardians of Obsolete Formats
characters.description: A group of anthropomorphic obsolete viewing formats dedicated to protecting their kind from being wiped out by newer formats. Breaking the Fellowship: "Format Wars II" shows Floppy Disk, Betamax, and Reel-to-Reel having gone their separate ways, presumably because of 8-Track's death, before being tracked down and reunited by Archie. Calling Your Attacks: All of them do this. Dwindling Party: 8-Track is killed in "The Last Laserdisc Player"; Betamax, Floppy Disk, Ampex Quadruplex, and Microfiche are killed in "Format Wars II"; and Reel-to-Reel and Black & White are killed in "Meet the Seer". Killed Off for Real: None of them survive to the end of the series.

characters.name: Principal Dean
characters.description: The principal of West Anderson High School, the school that Mordecai and Rigby went to. Hair-Trigger Temper: It doesn't take very much to set him off, especially when Rigby is involved. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Despite his animosity towards Rigby, he makes Ross give him one last chance to pass his science class, and he allows Rigby to re-enroll in school to get his diploma, even though heclearlydoesn't want to. Took a Level in Kindness: At first, he makes it clear through no uncertain terms that he wants Rigby to graduate just to get out of his school. As time goes on, Dean genuinely starts rooting for Rigby to succeed and even congratulates him when handing him his diploma.

characters.name: Moon Monster
characters.description: Generic Doomsday Villain: He primarily acts as a rampaging monster that wants to kill the park workers without any clear motives. Starter Villain: He is the show's first villain, not counting the Rock Paper Scissors demon seen in the pilot / "First Day". Uncertain Doom: Once the park workers escape the moon, the Moon Monster is left at the moon with no explanation as to what happened to him.

characters.name: Destroyer of Worlds
characters.description: Antagonist Title:In-Universe, it is the namesake for the Destroyer of Worlds arcade game. Back from the Dead:It, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". Beard of Evil: It has a moustache and goatee to go along with the whole Satan vibe. Big Red Devil: Resembles a pixelated version of an enlarged classic red devil face. Evil Laugh: Sometimes laughs as it's destroying things.

characters.name: Coffee Bean and Translator
characters.description: Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: The Coffee Bean only wears a pair of underwear and a white headband. Pokémon Speak: The Coffee Bean only says "coffee", requiring the Translator to translate for him. Even the contract they give Mordecai and Rigby is written in the Coffee Bean's "coffee" speak. This leads to Mordecai and Rigby not understanding them when they request the Fist Pump tickets as part of the contract and unwittingly signing them away. Smart People Wear Glasses: The Translator wears glasses and is smart enough to understand and translate what the Coffee Bean says. Torpedo Tits: The Coffee Bean can spew coffee from his nipples.

characters.name: Hot Dogs
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: Walking, talking hot dogs. Back from the Dead:They are among the villains revived in "Exit 9B". Black Comedy Cannibalism: The hot dogs start eating each other once they realize they taste really good with mustard. Hypocrite: For all their talk about wanting to avenge their fellow hot dogs being eaten, they have no qualms with eating each other once they get covered in mustard. I Lied: The lead hot dog told Rigby that they believe it is their destiny to be eaten, only for him to later admit it was a lie to get Rigby to let them out of the cooler.

characters.name: Unicorns
characters.description: Absurdicorn: The unicorns are an obnoxious group of unicorns that quickly outstay their welcome after being drawn to Dudetime cologne. They fart sparkles in Rigby's face and ruin the park by partying. Back from the Dead: They return in "House Rules" as part of the No Rules Man's realm. The Bully: They love to pick on non-Unicorns. Fierce Unicorn: They appear friendly at first, but they are soon revealed to be hyper-aggressive, obnoxious jerks who torment Rigby andeat Benson's gumballs after tying him up. Jerkass: Selfish, crude and violent.

characters.name: Master Prank Caller
characters.description: Ambiguously Human:His true form resembles a decrepit old human but given his phone suit and supernatural abilities it's not entirely clear if he's human. Animate Inanimate Object: His true form is a phone with human arms and legs.Although he turns out to really be a guy in a phone-like suit. Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". This was despite the fact that he was shown befriending Mordecai and Rigby at the end of his debut. However, the fact he appears right after the Stag-Man is knocked down could imply that the Prank Caller was the one who attacked him and was an ally to the Park, making it unclear which side he's on during this cameo. Cool Car: He summons a sleek black limousine for him to drive as he's chasing after Mordecai and Rigby in their cart. Disproportionate Retribution: Mordecai and Rigby making some bad attempts at prank calling him is enough to prompt him to send them both back in time and later try to kill them.

characters.name: Future Mordecai and Future Rigby
characters.description: Accent Slip-Up: They speak with British accents for most of the episode, only to slip back into their normal voices after their past-selves out them as frauds. Big "NO!": Both of them before Mordecair rips his band shirt, erasing them from existence. Broken Pedestal: Mordecai and Rigby think they're cool until they discover that they got to where they were by being lying douchebags; by rejecting a future built on lies, their future selves cease to exist. Cool Shades: They wear darkened sunglasses as part of their rocker look. Fake Brit: In-Universe. Mordecai and Rigby's future selves speak in fake, stereotypical British accents. They drop the act once Mordecai and Rigby refuse to start a music career by lip-synching.

characters.name: British Taxi
characters.description: An evil british taxi from a film that Rigby was watching that is now after him. Pokémon Speak: “Ello gov’nor” is the only thing it ever says. "Scooby-Doo" Hoax: An unintentional one. The haunted taxi turned out to be a video store clerk who was forced to wear that suit by his boss and was following Rigby because his video rental was overdue.

characters.name: Peeps
characters.description: A giant floating eyeball who is the owner of a surveillance camera company. Anti-Villain: He expresses the desire to harvest the park crew's eyes as trophies and isn't above cheating in a staring contest, but he sticks to theExact Wordsin his contract with Benson and upholds his end of the bargain with no strings attached. Exact Words: His lifetime contract for Jeepers Peepers X-Infinity provides surveillance 24/7, 365, with the only way to cancel it being if the signer dies. Eye Scream:The wager for his and Mordecai's staring contest is that Peeps is allowed to harvest the park crew's eyes if he wins.All of his eyes end up blinded by Rigby's laser pointer after Peeps tries to cheat in the staring contest.Peeps:(As he's being hauled into an ambulance)All I see is darkness! The wager for his and Mordecai's staring contest is that Peeps is allowed to harvest the park crew's eyes if he wins.

characters.name: Garrett Bobby Ferguson "GBF"
characters.description: A giant floating head with a beard held the universe record for an arcade game until Mordecai and Rigby beat his record. Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". Beard of Evil: A massive asshole with a thick beard. Big "NO!": When Mordecai and Rigby beat his record. Cephalothorax: A giant bearded head with limbs coming out of it.

characters.name: The Hammer
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: The Hammer's extremely tall height, blue skin and red eyes call his humanity into question. Ambiguous Situation: It's not clear whether the strange TV Mordecai and Rigby is itself malicious and brought the Hammer to life to attack them both, or if the Hammer is himself an evil entity who used the TV as a conduit to enter the real world. Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". The Dreaded: Infamous for being an incredibly hard boss to defeat. Final Boss:In-Universe, he's the last boss of theFighting GameMordecai and Rigby play.

characters.name: Susan
characters.description: Susan was hired by Mr. Maellard to replace Benson as the new park manager while Benson got demoted, when she turned out to be even worse than the two. Assimilation Plot: Her plan for managing The Park is to force everyone to work under her standards until they look just like her. Attack Its Weak Point: Her heels in her giant form. When broken, she can't stand and falls to her death. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Hertrueform. Back from the Dead:She, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B".

characters.name: Game Store Manager/"Darthon"
characters.description: Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". The GM Is a Cheating Bastard: When Mordecai and Rigby start to win at the Realm of Darthon, the Game Manager resorts to altering the rules in an attempt to disadvantage them both. Graceful Loser:As stubborn as he is in refusing to give Mordecai and Rigby a refund, he gives them back their money when they beat him fair and square in a game ofThe Realm of Darthon. Implausible Deniability: Even after Mordecai and Rigby point out all ofThe Realm of Darthon's blatant design flaws and poor product quality, he keeps doubling down on his belief that there's nothing wrong with it instead of just giving the duo a refund. Never My Fault: He refuses to admit there's anything wrong withThe Realm of Darthonas a game and insists that Mordecai and Rigby just aren't playing it right.

characters.name: Summertime Song
characters.description: When Rigby gets the song, "Summertime Loving, Loving in the Summer (Time)", stuck in his head and gets it out of his head, the song manifested itself into a physical form of a cassette tape and annoys everybody with its song. Animate Inanimate Object: It’s a giant cassette tape. Anthropomorphic Personification: A semi-physical manifestation of anEar Worm. Back from the Dead:It is brought back to life in "Exit 9B". Department of Redundancy Department: The song "Summertime Loving, Loving in the Summer (Time)".

characters.name: Doug "The Doppelganger" Shablowski
characters.description: An anthropomorphic otter whom Rigby hires as a temp to do his work for him, but turns out to be a con artist who can copy another person. Affably Evil: Outside of his attempts to impersonate, Doug is a legitimately hard-working and nice guy. Even as he's being arrested, he simply gives Rigby a sincere piece of advice by pointing out how much the raccoon has to be thankful for. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He comes off as friendly, optimistic, and hardworking, but deep down, he's a serial scammer stealing other peoples' identities throughout the nation. Ditto Fighter: Can transform into anyone and mimic their style trying to steal their life. Extreme Doormat: Played straight at first, as he doesn't seem to mind Rigby giving him all his work; but it's eventually subverted when he starts to copy Rigby's mannerisms and try to take over his life.

characters.name: Icedrom and Ygbir
characters.description: Evil Is Bigger: Much bigger than the real Mordecai and Rigby. Hat of Authority: They both wear top hats when showing they are the leaders.

characters.name: Ybgir
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: This monster attacks everyone in sightsuch as Rigby (despite the latter being the one to summon him)and random parkgoers as well. Beard of Evil: The hair on Ybgir's chin is grown out long, giving the impression of a beard. The Corruption: Can turn others into jinx demons by scratching them. Dark Is Evil: Black colored and very sinister. Determinator: Even though it stops to scratch and corruptanyonein sight, it still has its mind set on attacking Rigby.

characters.name: Zombies
characters.description: A group of zombies that are unwittingly reanimated by Mordecai and Rigby from the bodies laid to rest in the Park graveyard. All Part of the Show: Mordecai, Rigby and the other park workers are able to play them off as part of theZombie Apocalypsemovie the park was showing for movie night. Back from the Dead:They, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". Giant Mook: The zombie for Howard "Hellion" Fightington, a muscular bodybuilder. Groin Attack: Skips attempts to kick Howard in the balls.It doesn't work.

characters.name: Four-Armageddon, the Fire Marshall and Hissy Fit
characters.description: Berserk Button: Saying wrestling is fake really sets them off. Disproportionate Retribution: They attempt to brutally beat Mordecai and Rigby for saying wrestling is fake. Multi-Armed and Dangerous: Four-Armageddon has six arms, with two in place of his legs. Token Non-Human: Hissy Fit is the only one who's visibly not at all human, instead being a green lizard man. Walking Shirtless Scene: Being wrestlers, they're never seen wearing shirts and display their abs for all to see.

characters.name: Night Owl
characters.description: The Night Owl is a DJ that freezes Mordecai, Rigby, Muscle Man, and High-Five Ghost alive to become famous forever. Attention Whore: His whole plan is mostly for eternal fame. Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". The Bad Guy Wins: His plan went offperfectly, and when the gang wakes up decades later, he's built himself into a powerful businessman with his own high tech museum. This future is averted when they escape, and the Night Owl is left a penniless loser again. Big "NO!": Happens in poetic succession with both his future and past self, respectively before and after the gang prevent his contest from happening in the first place.

characters.name: Duck Collector
characters.description: Back from the Dead: Is one of the villains revived in Exit 9B. Bad People Abuse Animals: Whatever his intentions for the baby ducks were, they almost certainly weren't good given his willingness to kidnap them and how he had no problems shoving them in a tiny box. Bullying a Dragon: Threatening the baby ducks and their mother earns hima karate chop from the buff duck the baby ducks fuse into. Evil Old Folks: Seems to be an older person given his white hair. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: Wears glasses and is a malicious animal abuser.

characters.name: Warden of the Internet
characters.description: No Sense of Humor: Believes the Internet should be a serious place for communication and writing research papers, instead of viral videos. Wardens Are Evil: Runs a prison that locks up viral video makers. Wedgie: Receives (somehow) this from the Wedgie Ninja hard enough they explode.

characters.name: Were-Skunk
characters.description: A skunk who sprays Rigby, causing him to slowly turn into a skunk. Faking the Dead: What kickstarts the plot when Rigby was about to pick up what they assume to be roadkill, only for him to get sprayed by the Were-Skunk. Jerkass: Rude and abrasive to everyone he interacts with. This trait also gets passed onto Rigby after he slowly starts to become a skunk. Kick the Dog: Attempts to turn Rigby into a skunk purely out of spite and so he won't be the only were-skunk around. Our Werewolves Are Different: Has the bit of turning someone into their kind, in their case by spraying someone. And just like silver, they can only be slain by getting hitting them with tomato paste.

characters.name: Carrey O'Key and Carl
characters.description: The owner of a karaoke restaurant and his bouncer. The Brute: Carl is very big and muscular, befitting his job as a bouncer. Disproportionate Retribution: Mordecai and Rigby demanding the master tape of their karaoke performance is enough to make him ban them from his restaurant permanently and have them thrown out. Fat Bastard: Carrey is very portly and a jerkass. Punny Name: He's a karaoke bar owner whose name is a homophone for "karaoke."

characters.name: Order of the Blondes
characters.description: A group of blonde men who turn out to secretly be part of an evil organization. Affably Evil: They're an evil secret society, but they're polite and treat Mordecai with respect after he joins their fold, up until he refuses to kill Rigby by dipping him in blonde dye. Back from the Dead:They, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". Equal-Opportunity Evil: They look down on other hair colors, but they accept people of any ethnicity even if they're not natural blondes. Large and in Charge: TheKing Mookwho leads them is much larger than the other members.

characters.name: Stag-Man
characters.description: A half-human, half-deer man who hunts Mordecai, Rigby, Margaret and Eileen for camping in the forest. Back from the Dead: Is one of the villains revived in Exit 9B. Berserk Button: He hates Mordecai and Rigby for all the years they've camped in his territory and doing things he considers disrespectful to the forest. When their latest campout with Margaret and Eileen causes even more ruckus than usual, he snaps and tries to kill them. Deer in the Headlights:Fittingly, he meets his end when a car swerves and comes towards him as he stares in horror before he gets hit. Determinator: He can run fast enough to keep up with Margaret's car.

characters.name: Judge Broseph Chillaxton
characters.description: Awesome McCoolname: He's a "cool" judge, so of course he has a "cool" name like "Broseph Chillaxton." Back from the Dead:Is one of the villains revived in Exit 9B. Cool Shades: He's a "cool" judge, so of course he wears black shades on his (non-existent) face. The Faceless: Has no face or head to speak of. Felony Misdemeanor: Convicts Mordecai and Rigby for being "too cool."

characters.name: Cool Prosecutor
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: Looks human, but the square proportions on his face call it into question. Amoral Attorney: Uses various underhanded tactics in court, such as getting Mordecai and Rigby say "I swear" while placing their hands on a book before using it as evidence of them admitting to using swear words and thus being "cool." Cool Shades: Wears black shades, like everyone else in the Cool Court. Evil Wears Black: Wears a black turtleneck. Uncertain Doom: We don't see what happened to him, but given how he was likely on the space station when it exploded he likely didn't survive.

characters.name: No Rules Man
characters.description: This mysterious man lives in a place where rules literally do not exist. Anarchy Is Chaos: He exists to teach Mordecai and Rigby how a world without any rules can lead to chaos. He revels in being a jerk because there's nothing saying that he can't act the way he does. Back from the Dead: After being killed at the end of "House Rules,"he reappears in "Exit9B" as part of GBF Jr.'s army. Berserk Button: Telling him what to do. Big "NO!":When he's all alone playing video games and a new rule comes down saying, "No Video Games" causing him to die.

characters.name: Crew Crew
characters.description: The Bully: They make fun of Pops even though he only complimented their rhyming abilities. Five-Man Band: A villainous variant. Alpha Dog, the leader, is theBig Bad. Blitz Comet isThe Dragon. Demel-Ishun isthe lone female. V-Tron, who handles their equipment, is theEvil Genius. And Francois isThe Brute. Foil: To Pops. Both they and Pops are skilled at rhyming, but while Pops uses his poetry to express positive emotions about things,CrewCrewonly mock and insult people even when they're not rapping. Sorting Algorithm of Evil: Mordecai and Rigby rap against Blitz Comet and Demel-Ishun before Pops faces off against Alpha Dog, the leader and most skilled among them. Token Minority: V-Tron is the only white member of the crew.

characters.name: Park Avenue
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object:His true identity is a spray can with arms and legs. In the Hood: Wears a black hood that obscures his identity.He turns out to be a giant walking spray can. Maker of Monsters: He spray paints monsters and brings them life to attack Mordecai and Rigby. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Based onBanksy, given his mysterious identity, anti-authority attitude that he expresses through his art, and him insulting Benson as a "bourgeois sucka". Small Name, Big Ego: He proudly claims to be a rebel for the masses when in reality, all he's doing is leaving behind a mess with his art that causes more trouble than good.Park Avenue:Yeah, that's right, I'm the one who did it!I'mthe graffiti artist! I'm hitting the world with knowledge! I'm painting the truth! I'm painting rebellion! I—Benson:Iam calling the cops.

characters.name: Doom Ma Geddon Virus
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: It's a powerful virus, but it's still beholden to speed of the computer it's inhabiting. As such,opening up a bunch of applications causes it to slow it down, giving Skips an opportunity to destroy the computer. Contagious A.I.: It's a computer virus that looks and behaves like a biological virus. Digital Abomination: It's a sentient computer virus that behaves like a bacteriophage.

characters.name: Eggscellent Manager
characters.description: Good All Along:It turns out the reason he and the other restaurant employees. attempted to stop Mordecai from completing the Eggscellenet challenge is because the final step of the challenge involves a life or death decision. Walking Spoiler: It's difficult to talk about his role in the episode without spoiling the fact thatunlike most other antagonists in the series, heisn't actually evil. Well-Intentioned Extremist:He attempts to use force to stop Mordecai from finishing the omelet, but only to keep his life from being at risk. It's implied this is due to the fact that the previous person who succeeded in eating the omelet, Jonathan Kimble, never returned. Wham Line: After Mordecai finishes the omelet before the manager can stop him."Oh no, we were only trying to help."

characters.name: The Urge
characters.description: Back from the Dead:He, along with a plethora of villains who died due to Mordecai and Rigby's actions, came back in "Exit 9B". Evil Is Hammy: Even when he's tracking down and trying to kill Rigby/Trash Boat, he can't help but vocalize as a reminder that he's a rock star.There you aaaaare! Fat Bastard: The Urge has become morbidly obsse and balding in the future. He also tries to kill Rigby for upstaging him instead of simply letting him change his name back. Formerly Fit: The Urge in the present isslim, handsome, and well-fit. When The Urge from the future comes to kill Rigby/Trash Boat, he ismorbidly obeseand balding. I Was Quite a Looker: The Urge has let himself go after "Trash Boat" upstaged him, losing all of his good looks and physique.

characters.name: Klorgbane the Destroyer
characters.description: The evil brother of the Guardians of Eternal Youth. Only vulnerable to the Fists of Justice, he returns every 157 years to do battle with Skips. Arch-Enemy: To Skips; he killed his first love, Mona, is the main reason Skips chose immortality, and returns once every 157 years to battle him. Ax-Crazy: He is a violent, sadistic being. Big Brother Bully: To the Guardians of Eternal Youth, solely by being evil. He outrightkillsArchibald during his battle with Skips. The Bully: He was this in high school and nobody stood up to him due to being huge and immortal until Skips came along. Headmaster Bennett was unaware of his bullying until he saw his true colors during prom.

characters.name: Thomas (the son of Death)
characters.description: An infantile demon who is the son of Death. Accents Aren't Hereditary: Though his father was an English-accented being, Thomas has a rugged American accent as an adult. Baby Talk: Thomas does this only when his parents are around to keep up the charade that he's still young. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: To his parents, he's an angel. To everyone else, he's batshit insane. Bratty Half-Pint: He's very short and is extremely spoiled.

characters.name: Maitre 'd
characters.description: Berserk Button: Do not fake being fancy in his restaurant. In fact, don't evenbothershowing up if you can't line up with his unnecessarily high standards. Big Bad: Him putting down Muscle Man for his lack of etiquette kicks off the latter's insecurities in "Fancy Restaurant". He becomes more active later down the episode, exposing and trying to kill him, his date Starla and her family, and Mordecai and Rigby for faking Muscle Man's fanciness. Disney Villain Death:Thrown out a window and onto a car, leaving him heavily injured. Subverted when he makes a later cameo, revealing he survived. Disproportionate Retribution: Attempts to force Muscle Man out of his restaurant just for choosing the wrong spoon, even though up until that point he had behaved perfectly in line with the bistro's etiquette. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": He is only known as "Maitre d'", even in the credits.

characters.name: Death Bear
characters.description: Ambiguously Evil: Supposedly, it attacked and killed its trainer out of nowhere, but it's unclear whether that's actually what happened or just an urban legend. It attacks Mordecai, Rigby, Margaret and Eileen when they enter its enclosure, but it's unclear if that was out of maliciousness or if it viewed them as intruders on its territory. Bears Are Bad News: A bear with a feared reputation built up around it after it (according to urban legend) killed its trainer out of nowhere. The Dreaded: Anyone called "Death Bear" isn't someone you should take lightly. The Juggernaut: Chases the four from the zoo all the way back to the park house, with few obstacles being able to slow it down, and shrugs off about a hundred or so tranquilizer darts before finally going down. Mysterious Past: Aside from living in the abandoned Park Zoo for decades, we never learn about the rest of his origins. We don't know if it really attacked and killed its trainer out of nowhere or if it was just an urban legend, why he wants to kill people, nor do we learn about how he knows martial arts.

characters.name: Capicola Gang
characters.description: A group of living audio-animatronic that are criminals. The gang consist of two bears, one that resembles a bear and is also the leader and the other one that barely resembles a bear named Louie, and a female duck named J.B '70s Hair: J.B has a stereotypical 1970s afro haircut. Afro Asskicker: J.B has an afro haircut and fights ruthlessly. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Sentient animatronics that are gangsters with criminal careers. Bears Are Bad News: Two of the members are bears.

characters.name: The Contractor
characters.description: Avenging the Villain:His true goal turns out to be to resurrect his father and avenge his defeat by Mordecai and Rigby. Not only that he revives most of the other villains Mordecai and Rigby have faced so they can get their revenges as well.. Bad Boss: Extremely cruel to both Benson (whom he brainwashed to be his right-hand man) and Thomas, treating them both like slaves and repeatedly telling them they're expendable. Bastard Bastard:Most likely a bastard given that GBF Sr. said he never had a wife, and he's just as obnoxious and mean as his dad was. Beard of Evil: Has a rather bushy beard.In fact it's the same beard type as his father. Big Bad: Of "Exit 9B", which involves him buying the park in order to demolish it to make way for Exit 9B.

characters.name: Promise Pie
characters.description: Brutal Honesty: ItsAchilles' Heelis Mordecai and Rigby telling the contestants he ate what they really think of their pies, which causes them to be thrown out of Promise Pie and Promise Pie to shrink. Deal with the Devil: Unable to tell all the pie contestants what they think of their pies, with some of their pies tasting really bad, Mordecai and Rigby accept its offer to help them judge the contest. It's unclear exactly why he needs their consent to do this, but it does mean that telling each person the truth expels them from his body. Diabolus ex Nihilo: It's not clear at all where Promise Pie came from. He just suddenly appears in a trash can and offers to help Mordecai and Rigby with their dilemma. Evil Sounds Deep: His squeaky voice is actually an affectation, his natural voice sounding demonically deep, which really should have tipped Mordecai and Rigby off. Exact Words: Tells Mordecai and Rigby he'll help by "lowering the competition", which he does so by eating everyone he can.

characters.name: Quillgin
characters.description: Apple of Discord: Quillgin created an empty box that when opened will give whoever opens it what they desire the most. However, the key component used in making the box wasBlack Magic, which brought out the worst in people and made them fight over it. It was because of this that Santa ordered the box to be locked away and all research pertaining to it destroyed, kickstarting Quillgin's plan to retrieve his creation and use it to destroy Christmas as revenge. Big Bad: Of "The Christmas Special." Dramatically Missing the Point: After learning that its corrupting influence stemmed from being made using dark magic, Santa deemed the box to be too dangerous to give as a gift. Quillgin however failed to understand this and instead accused Santa of destroying his life's work because he feared the box would replace him.Quillgin:It didn't have to end this way, but you ruined my dream! If we made a box for everyone, then no one would be fighting over them. Did you ever think of that!? Ha! I bet you did. "If everyone had everything they wanted, then why would they need Santa?"Santa:It's not like that, Quillgin!Quillgin:Enough! You ruined my life's work, now I'm gonna ruin yours. Family-Friendly Firearms:Averted. He carries a real-life handgun that he uses to shoot Santa (who fortunately was wearing a bulletproof vest at the time) and threaten the park crew with, and has a hand grenade that he uses to try and blow them up with when he loses his gun. The Grinch: Quite possiblyone of the most evil and dangerous examples of this trope.Not only does he want to destroy Christmas, he plans tokill anyone who celebrates the holidaysimply because Santa rightfully rejected his idea for a gift.

characters.name: Hector
characters.description: The owner of the "South of the Line Chile Rellenos" and an underground fireworks dealer. Beard of Evil: Has a goatee and runs an illegal drug- er...gunpowderoperation. The Cartel: His whole "Chile Rellenos" operation, which involves him having gunpowder illegally put in the Chile Rellenos to up their spiciness, is very reminiscent of a Mexican drug cartel. Family-Friendly Firearms:Played With. He wields what's obviously an AK-47, but loads it up with a firework rather than ammo. I Can't Believe It's Not Heroin!: Him filling his Chile Rellenos with gunpowder to increase their spiciness is treated like an illegal drug operation, with it even being mentioned as illegal by the FDA.

characters.name: Geese
characters.description: Four Canadian Geese who seek to claim the park as their territory by attacking anybody who gets in their way. All Your Powers Combined: When the four fuse. Arch-Enemy: They constantly state how they and the Baby Ducks are sworn enemies. Armored Villains, Unarmored Heroes: In the first part of the fight, but it's subverted when the ducks gain aPowered Armor. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Like the baby ducks, they can also fuse together to be a giant four-headed goose man.

characters.name: Mitsuru Shinehara
characters.description: The host of the Japanese game show,Fool Me Once, Shame on You! Fool Me Twice, I Punch Your Face!. Ax-Crazy: He's not what you would call sane, considering his sadistic streak and obsession with punching people's faces. Hidden Disdain Reveal: He's a host for a game show where the contestants try to trick him three times, and reveals that he actually genuinelyhatesliars. Hoist by His Own Petard: Due to being successfully fooled three times by the Park workers, his fist literally turns on him to punch his face in. Megaton Punch: His punches aren't just painful, he's hospitalized and permanently deformed many people. When he goes too long without punching a face, his hand enlarges and is capable of extending on his arm to punch far away targets, hitting hard enough to generate shockwaves.

characters.name: The Wickets
characters.description: Berserk Button: The Wickets really don't like cell phones. They also don't take well to any disrespect towards croquet. Determinator: When you break the no cell phone rule they will chase you to death since they followed Mordecai the whole time on the way to the airport. Disproportionate Retribution: The Wickets don't like cellphones and warn Mordecai against using them on their turf. They decide to murder him when he disobeys their orders. Karmic Death: The Wickets meet their end by crashing into a billboard thatadvertises cell phones.

characters.name: Stress Monster
characters.description: Dark Is Evil: The monster is pitch-black and wants nothing more than to kill those who brought it into existence. The Heartless: Made from the park workers' stress. Red Eyes, Take Warning: All five heads have glowing red eyes.

characters.name: Cool Cubed and Translator
characters.description: A giant slushie cup and his translator who seek to completely and permanently freeze over Thomas's brain. Anthropomorphic Personification: Of the effects of the Cool Cubed's brain freeze. Ax-Crazy: Both of them are shown to be rather violent and sadistic individuals. The Cool Cubed especially stands out since he's basically trying to murder Thomas for the sake of upholding his reputation as the coldest slushie in the world. Disney Villain Death: The translator bites it when his attempt at impaling the mind version of Thomas causes the glacier to crack, causing him to fall to his doom. Freeze Ray: The Cool Cubed is able to fire these out of the straw sticking out of the top of his head.

characters.name: Frank Jones
characters.description: A health inspector who seeks to condemn Muscle Man's trailer so he can take it for himself. Disney Villain Death: He dies plummeting down on a cliff, shouting aBig "NO!"from being had by Muscle Man after discovering the trailer isn't in the truck he is on. Evil Is Petty: The fact that he impersonated a health inspector to take away Muscle Man's home over a hotdog eating contest really shows the lengths of his revenge scheme. Kick the Dog: Played straight initially as Frank not only threatens to send Muscle Man's trailer to the dump and get it scrapped, but when he gives him and his friends a whole day to spruce the trailer, Franks starts to destroy parts of Muscle Man's trailer, from the windows to his door. Subverted, however, as Muscle Man eventually stands up to Frank bydecking him in the face. Sore Loser: Frank was the runner-up in the hotdog eating contest Muscle Man won his trailer from. He accuses Muscle Man of cheating back then by mushing his hot dogs together with water and that the trailer should've been his, only for Muscle Man to retort that it was totally a fair move and that the Japanese do it all the time.

characters.name: Country Club
characters.description: Acrofatic: Even though the leader is obese and spends all his time sitting down, don't let that fool you; he was very capable of fighting Mordecai and Rigby thanks to being immune to pain from having many facial surgeries and having tiger tendons in his hands. Ambiguous Situation: It is unknown if the Country Club Leader died of oxygen deprivation upon being launched into space or if he is still able to breathe.. And I Must Scream: The Country Club Leader is turned into a toilet and launched into space.Presumably if he can survive in space, he’ll float as a sentient porcelain asteroid of all eternity. Asshole Victim: The Country Club Leader is turned into a toilet and launched into space. Assuming he will die of oxygen deprivation, no one mourns him besides his followers as he and his cronies enjoyed picking on the park workers. Badass Army: They’re composed of a leader with plastic surgery that makes him almost immune to pain, horse polo riders, muscular security guards and divers, a fisticuffs fighter, and a tennis ball launcher guy. All this makes them into a powerful army strong enough to hold their own against the park workers.

characters.name: DougMcFarlandand his employees
characters.description: The Ace: Discussed as Doug claims to be the "World's Best Boss" and has the "World's Best Employees". This is shown well as they managed to take down to park workers with ease before Benson's arrival in helping the latter win. Asshole Victim: Doug iskilled when Benson punches him one of his own delivery trucks as the former accidentally lands on the emergency brake lever and the accelerator, causing the truck to drive and crash into another truck. Seeing how Doug wanted the park workers dead, he's not going to be worth mourning at all. Ax-Crazy: Doug and his crew aren’t the most gentle villains. Doug is willing to punch the first guy he sees when introducing himself and his employees are more than willing to put up a violent fight against other employees. Badass Crew: Doug and his employees are extremely competent fighters. This is shown when the employees begin flooring Pops, Muscle Man, and even Skips, three of the strongest park workers. But once Benson comes to help, they all go down. Badass Normal: While lacking special abilities like other supernatural enemies the park has faced, these guys mainly use their incredible fighting skills and even office machinery for combat.

characters.name: Silver Dude
characters.description: Enemy Mime:Gets turned into a mime when being sent to street jail. Greed: He steals Mordecai and Rigby's songs because he wants all the money from their act all for himself. Hate Sink: Silver Dude is one of the show's villains who had absolutely no redeeming qualities. He shamelessly steals other peoples' songs (primarily Mordecai and Rigby), remixes them and does it along with a basic ball trick. To make it worse, Silver Dude claims that Mordecai and Rigby are the ones stealing his act. In the challenge, Silver Dude continues to remix Mordecai and Rigby's songs with his boombox until they destroy it. Silver Dude proves himself to be a horrible rapper with no musical talent of his own,but instead of accepting his loss, he tries to take the money for himself.Why did he do all these terrible things?Simply because he was a greedy scumbag who had no qualms stealing the talents of others to get money. Jerkass: He copies other peoples' acts, while claiming that he's not ripping them off. And he doesn't care at all. Laser-Guided Karma:When he gets angry and tries to take the money during a street performing battle, he gets sent to Street Jail.

characters.name: Rich Buckner
characters.description: The owner of Buck-Mart superstores, who seeks to obtain the rights to Thanksgiving via a wish-granting golden wishbone obtained from a naturally born turducken. Big Bad: Of "The Thanksgiving Special". Corrupt Corporate Executive: He's the megalomaniacal owner of a huge superstore chain who seeks to obtain the rights to Thanksgiving any way he can. One of the things he also hopes to obtain from wishing on the golden wishbone is an untraceable Swiss bank account. Disney Owns This Trope: He wants to obtain the rights to Thanksgiving so that he'll be the one everyone gives thanks to during the holiday. But because he can't legally buy it, he tries using a golden wishbone from a naturally born turducken to wish for it instead. Entitled Bastard: The reason he wants to own the rights to Thanksgiving is because he runs a successful business that employs thousands of workers, yet claims to never receive any thanks (giving) for it due to everyone "being too busy with their families".

characters.name: Bert Coleman
characters.description: The eccentric and mean-spirited host of "Expert Or Liar", a gameshow that makes people answer certain questions or be humiliated on national television. Eaten Alive: After answering the final question of the video game round correctly, Rigby punches him while declaring himself an expert, knocking Bert off his floating platform and right into the mouth of a pixelated Garrett Bobby Ferguson copy, which explodes shortly after. Hate Sink: Even by this series' standards, he's so in-your-face odious you'll feel like cheering when Rigby punches him out. Hypocrite: He loves exposing his contestants as "liars", while disguising himself and tricking them onto his show in a very dishonest way. Inexplicably Awesome: He seems like a normal man at first, but then he shows the ability to warp people to other dimensions based on the subject of his trivia. Given the presence of beings with similar powers, he might be just another otherworldly entity.

characters.name: The Sheriff
characters.description: A power abusing deputy who likes to imprison anyone he sees. Beard of Evil: He has a mustache and is a huge jerk. The Bully: Loves picking on the inmates he locks up and sprays them with a hose if they try to defy him. Crazy-Prepared: For some reason he has spare weapons hidden in hisjail cellafter the crew locked him inside to escape. Dirty Cop: He’s a cop who loves locking up people sees on the highway he patrols.

characters.name: MatchmakerMcIntyre
characters.description: A romantic cowboy and owner of the famous website "Couple Corral". Alliterative Name:MatchmakerMcIntyre. Beware the Silly Ones: This silly romantic cowboy tries to kill CJ with a bazooka at the end. Gone Horribly Right: His website really brought together the perfect couples... but with no one left to subscribe. Hate Sink: He harasses Mordecai to break up with CJ so he could return to his place and goes as far as to try to kill CJ with a bazooka. It's clear the writers made him as obnoxious and dangerous as a romantic roadblock could get for Mordecai.

characters.name: Joanne Hanatronic
characters.description: Eileen's roommate, who treats her like garbage and flips out over anyone touching her own stuff. Animal Motifs: To donkeys. Rigby calls her a donkey, her face is somewhat long like a donkey, her big hair somewhat resemble donkey ears, her deep voice resembles an donkey's bray, and she has pet horses (animals that resemble donkeys).
