Berserk Button:Don'ttouch her TV. She'll appear all of a sudden and threaten you. Big Eater: Implied. Rigby mentions that Joanne ate Eileen's whole jar of peanut butter. Catchphrase: "I'll X! And by that, I mean Y!"It apparently runs in her familyif her grandfather also saying it is any indication.

characters.name: Youth Topia
characters.description: A spa that uses turtles to achieve eternal youth. Bad People Abuse Animals: They harvest baby turtles and use them to achieve eternal youth, apparently sucking their own youth away in the process. There's also a group that do push-upsonthe turtles. Dirty Cop: There are two police officers who are in on the whole thing and arrest Mordecai and CJ when they try to interfere. Jerkass: Aside from abusing turtles for their own gain, they mock the gang for not having memberships to their spa. No Body Left Behind: They're all reduced to nothing by the baby turtles that Eileen freed.

characters.name: The Internet (Streaming)
characters.description: A giant and immensely powerful AI that embodies the internet. It seeks to obliterate all other video platforms to leave itself as the unchallenged format. Achilles' Heel: The Internet's first form is a data tower. Once it's destroyed, Internet loses its connection and powers down. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: It's a cold and unfeeling entity that solely desires domination over everything online. Anthropomorphic Personification: Of the internet, obviously, and more specifically, streaming services. Like the Guardians of Obsolete Formats and Disc family, it's a robotic humanoid with format based powers. Arc Villain: It appears any time the Format Wars are involved.

characters.name: Rich Steve
characters.description: A corrupt corporate executive looking for a very powerful suit. Bad Boss: Rich Steve shows this when he orders his men to blow themselves up in the tailors shop just to make a point. Entitled to Have You: Rich Steve feels like he is owed the Suit after having commissioned it from the "Worlds' Greatest Tailor" and only paid a measly $10 for it instead of the original price. Jerkass: Showcased early when the tailor asks for payment for creating the suit for him, only for Steve to welch on their agreement. Tanks for Nothing: He attempts to kill Benson in order to claim the suit with a tank, only for him to be sent flying with the tank he is still on, making the tank blow up with him.

characters.name: Jerry
characters.description: Sensei's apprentice who is secretly after Sensei's stomach transplant to replace his after his own got destroyed from eating Sensei's unhealthy experimental Death Sandwiches. A Pupil of Mine Until He Turned to Evil: He betrays everyone when he manages to get close to the stomach he needs. Didn't Think This Through: After knocking out the doctor who refused to do the operation and the nurse being unable to do so since that's not their area of expertise, he attempts to do it by himself, starting by... anesthetizing himself. He gets up when Mordecai and Rigby catch up to him, but is too woozy to do anything and is easily defeated. Evil All Along: At first he is just a guy who helps Mordecai and Rigby get to the special stomach needed for Sensei. But as soon the master is about to hand it over, he kills him and steals it, showing his true colors. Never My Fault: He blames Sensei for making his stomach explode from the Death Sandwiches Sensei was making, even though he warned him not to raid the vault.

characters.name: Randall Ross
characters.description: The main antagonist of theThe Movie, he was Mordecai and Rigby's old science teacher (who likewise coached vollyball on the side) who, in the future, now controls the Timenado and intends to wipe out all of existence. Alliterative Name:RandallRoss. And I Must Scream:Suffers this fate thanks to his own technology. After being decapitated, his time-collar resets to when his head expires, forcing him to die over and over,in an infinite loop.Even worse, he's swept away as a helpless head into the Timenado, doomed to sail through the timestream while unable to ever die. Thankfully, this is presumably averted when theBad Futureis aborted. Big Bad: OfThe Movie. Combat Pragmatist: Utilizes his teleportation in combat.

characters.name: Francis Jablonski
characters.description: Mordecai and Rigby's (mainly Rigby) old high school bully, who also becomes Rigby's new gym teacher when he's trying to get his high school diploma. The Bully: Was Mordecai and Rigby's (mainly Rigby) main bully when they were in high school. Heel–Face Turn: Appears to have pulled one as of the end of "Gymblonski". Jerk Jock: Jablonski is your stereotypical high school jock.

characters.name: Dr. Dome
characters.description: A scientist in charge of the dome and the main antagonist of The Dome Experiment Special. Large Ham: He has an exaggerated German accent and all of his lines are very over-the-top. Meaningful Name: His name is Dr. Dome, and he is the lead scientist of the Dome Experiment. Pungeon Master: Much of his dialogue involves changing words to "dome", most noticably with "don't". Uncertain Doom: The last time we see him, he's frozen by his own weather control booth. It's never confirmed whether or not he died.

characters.name: David
characters.description: Cain and Abel: He's the Cain to Gary's Abel. Cold Ham: While his dialogue is rather emotional, his tone is extremely subdued. Creative Sterility: David is a talented player, but he sticks only to simple patterns and it's implied he can't master any "challenging" music, hence his banning of it. Deader than Dead: After his physical form is disintegrated by the sun, the disk containing his information is destroyed by two rebels he previously sentenced to be executed. Graceful Loser: After Gary bests him with discord music, he calmly accepts his defeat while being launched into the sun.

characters.name: The Cube Bros
characters.description: Beard of Evil: Andy has a beard and is a villain. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first they seem nice but they're actually evil robots. Fat Bastard: Andy has a plump built and is a malicious android. Lean and Mean: Randy is quite skinny and has an evil personality. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: They somewhat resemble human versions of Mordecai, Rigby, and Hi Five Ghost. Randy's slim build makes him similar to Mordecai. Andy's brown color scheme makes him look like Rigby. Gill has a hairstyle that makes him look like Hi Five Ghost.

characters.name: Dr. Langer
characters.description: Ambiguously Evil: It's unclear from the start what his exact motivations are and whether or not he's acting with or against the park crew.He turns out to be helping prepare Pops for his battle with Anti-Pops. Pet the Dog: He comforts Mr. Maellard asthe park is launched into space with Maellard's son, Pops, on it. Signing-Off Catchphrase: "Langer out!" Troll: Messes with Benson and the park crew about the button, and has a habit of flying away with his jetpack to avoid indulging any information.

characters.name: Brobots/Reaperbots
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first they appear willing to help the Park Crew return to Earth, when in reality they were harvesting their resources to sell on the black market, their fake and real names define this trope.

characters.name: Bounty Hunter
characters.description: Harmless Freezing: The bounty hunter's gun does this. A store employee is even able to talk in this condition and just needs someone else to break the ice open. This is because the bounty hunter is trying to bring Pops in alive, though it's unclear if it would be harmless to anyone from Earth. Hoist by His Own Petard: The bounty hunter is defeated by being locked in a display case, wield shut by her own ice gun. Implied Death Threat: All the grief pursuing the crew takes a personal toll on the bounty hunter.Bounty Hunter:Even without those beds, I'll make sure you get a good night's sleep! Jerkass: When an employee informs her she has to bus her tray at the store's cafe. She freezes him instantly. Later when the employee complains to his manager about it. She does it again to both of them. Near-Villain Victory: The bounty hunter would have succeeded in capturing our heroes had the store employees not intervened about the aforementioned complaint.

characters.name: Valencia
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She presents herself as very energetic and charismatic, but it's quite obvious that she is only out to make sure that the coffee shop loses all its business. Villainous Breakdown: She doesnottake it well when Eileen and Margaret destroy the last of the fusion logs before she could get the recipe.

characters.name: Talks
characters.description: Berserk Button: Being told what to do and being ordered to do work around the park. Blob Monster: When he loses it after being told to do something by Benson, he turns into a giant monster made of acidic toxic goop. Cool Shades: Wears a pair of sunglasses perched over his head. Dirty Coward: He even somewhat lampshades it as he loves busting the chops of everyone at the park except for Skips, as he says he wouldn't do that to someone bigger and stronger than him. Fat Bastard: He has a stocky build and is a moochingJerkassthat constantly takes jabs at his co-workers that he downplays by saying that he's "just busting their chops".

characters.name: Blake
characters.description: Jerk Jock: He was designed to a professional volleyball player and has quite an assertive, unsportsmanlike attitude. Pec Flex: He is introduced doing this when Dan is describing him to Muscle Man.

characters.name: Stiltwalkers
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Initially they (besides Jefferson) welcome Rigby with open arms, but the moment Uncle Sam demands to be given $12,000 dollars their true colors begin to show. Furthermore, like everyone else Uncle Sam tells Rigby that his "giant eating sushi" picture idea stinks Fantastic Slurs: They refer to anyone who doesn't use stilts as "groundies". Faux Affably Evil: Uncle Sam still tries to put up a friendly façade when asking Rigby for $12,000. But when Rigby asks if it’s a scam and refuses, the façade begins to fade.
